memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.'" - Ex 20:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The setting of this command is a courtroom. In ancient Israel there were no
forensic tools; cases turned on witnesses. A lying witness could destroy an
innocent person completely.

That is why God takes it so seriously. Naboth lost his vineyard and his life
because two men were paid to lie (1 Kgs 21). Jesus Himself was condemned on false
testimony (Matt 26:59-60).

But the principle runs wider than courtrooms. It covers gossip, the selective
detail that creates a false impression, the shared story we never verified, the
silence that lets a wrong impression stand.

Notice the phrase "against your neighbour." Words have targets. Something is
being done to a real person when we speak carelessly about them.

We live in an age where a false report can circle the world in hours and the
correction never catches up. Forwarding a message we have not checked is a
modern form of this ancient sin.

Paul's alternative is simple: "speaking the truth in love" (Eph 4:15). Both
words matter. Truth without love wounds. Love without truth flatters. Together
they build people up.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you passed on something about someone without verifying it?
2. Does your speech about absent people build them up or diminish them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, guard my tongue. Make me a person whose word can be trusted and whose
speech protects others. Amen.
